newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW sets more grain export records.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW sets more grain export records.

text.p: Australia's New South Wales grain co-operative GrainCorp Ltd had broken every Australian grain shipping record in April and now expected to export a massive 6.5 million tonnes of grain from its two port terminals this year, it said in a statement.
This was more than double the previous record, it said.
An all-time record of 718,562 tonnes of grain were shipped from GrainCorp ports at Newcastle and Port Kembla in March, almost doubling average shipping months, it said.
April exports topped half a million tonnes and similar shipping figures were expected for the remainder of the year, it said.
"GrainCorp is on target to break all exporting records this year," managing director Tom Keene said.
In the last week of April, seven ships were loaded from Port Kembla in only seven days, 179,000 tonnes of wheat and the most grain ever shipped in one week from an Australian terminal, Keene said.

The record 1996/97 harvest saw a record high of 8.5 million tonnes of grain delivered into the GrainCorp system, while extended working arrangements had moved an average 632,000 tonnes of grain from country sites each month, he said.
